blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how sentences are formed? Understanding the basic structure of sentences is essential for effective communication.

blocks.markdown: A simple sentence consists of a subject, a verb, and sometimes an object. The subject tells us who or what the sentence is about, while the verb indicates the action or state of being.

blocks.title: Key Terms
blocks.text: 1. **Subject**: The person or thing that performs the action. 2. **Verb**: The action word in the sentence. 3. **Object**: The receiver of the action.

blocks.markdown: For example, in the sentence 'Chinonso eats rice,' 'Chinonso' is the subject, 'eats' is the verb, and 'rice' is the object. Not all simple sentences need an object, such as 'Chinonso runs.'

blocks.title: Identifying Components of a Simple Sentence
blocks.prompt: Identify the subject and verb in the following sentence: 'Ada plays football.'

steps.text: Step 1: Look for the subject. In this case, 'Ada' is the one performing the action.
Step 2: Identify the verb. Here, 'plays' is the action being performed.

blocks.markdown: When writing a simple sentence, always start with a capital letter and end with a full stop. For example, 'Emeka loves to read.'

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always check your sentences for proper capitalization and punctuation before submitting your work.

points: A simple sentence consists of a subject, verb, and sometimes an object.
Always start with a capital letter and end with a full stop.
